blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Addresses with non-ASCII characters are logged in full or partly unmasked) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The pattern accepts only ASCII in the local part and the domain, so an address the proposal promises to mask reaches the logs kept 90 days by the hosting provider (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 32). `logInfo("signup", { email: "josé@exemple.fr" })` writes `josé@exemple.fr` unchanged (the character before `@` is outside the class, so nothing matches); `ada@münchen.de` is not matched either; `zoë.martin@example.org` becomes `zoë.***@example.org`, leaking the first name. Match on Unicode letters (`\p{L}\p{N}` with the `u` flag) in both the local part and the domain, or mask any token containing `@`, and add tests for a non-ASCII local part and an IDN domain.
findings.title: Addresses with non-ASCII characters are logged in full or partly unmasked

findings.recommendation: For a personal or small-company domain (`a***@lovelace.family`), the first letter plus the domain can still identify the customer, so the log line stays personal data (GDPR Art. 4(1), Art. 5(1)(c)). Whether such domains appear in the logs could not be verified; if they do, replace the whole address with a fixed token or a keyed hash when correlation is needed.
findings.title: The masked form keeps the domain and first letter
